lines.text: For it is the curse of a life which is so feverishly hurried that
the pauses which do occasionally arise are void of content.
At such times a terrible boredom may overcome him; he
may suddenly be seized by a questioning as to the meaning
of his life and feel mounting within him a disgust which can
even lead to suicide.
"In Him we live and move and have our being." Whoever
lives with the feeling of emptiness and tedium has ceased to
realize this truth. If he is courageous enough to reflect, he
will of course become aware that it is precisely in the sense
of void which oppresses him that God is speaking to him and
asking him questions: questioning him about himself and
calling him to account as to what he has made of his life.
But can man face such questions? The organization of life
has discovered the means of enabling man to deal with these
moments of emptiness and tedium: amusement and dis-
traction, pleasure and noise! Man is to forget the shattering
truth: "In Him we live and move and have our being!"
But what is operative in this frenzied effort to become
absorbed in bustle and noise but that original fear of life
which man seeks so desperately to still?
Technology, which was intended to subjugate the energies
of nature and harness to his service the forces which man
once felt to be daemonic and crushing, has itself become a
daemonic power compelling man to serve itself and thus
bringing him to lose his own soul.
It would of course be a foolish mistake to try to wage war
against the technical resources which we all need for our
lives. It is rather a question of making it clear to ourselves
that technics can be used for both good and evil, and that
it confronts us with a powerful temptation. Against this
temptation we must fight; if we succumb to it, then tech-
nology assumes the character of the daemonic and robs us
of our true life in God. The temptation is that the very
success of technology may lead us to believe that our life is
secure and to lose the sense of its frailty; to regard ourselves
as master of our life and to benumb man's original fear of life
instead of allowing the latter to drive him on to seek his God.
